easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “David spake unto the LORD the words of this song.”
easy.q: To whom did David speak the words of this song?

easy.explanation: The LORD delivered David from all his enemies and from Saul.
easy.q: From whose hand had the LORD delivered David?

answers: As his rock, fortress, and deliverer
easy.explanation: David says, “The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer.”
easy.q: How does David first describe the LORD?

answers: Because the LORD is worthy to be praised and saves him
Because he wants a new fortress
Because he is preparing a feast
medium.explanation: David calls on the LORD, who is worthy to be praised, and says he will be saved from his enemies.
medium.q: Why does David call upon the LORD?

medium.explanation: Each image presents the LORD as David’s protector and refuge.
medium.q: What do the images of a rock, fortress, shield, and high tower have in common?

medium.explanation: A refuge is a safe place to which someone may flee for protection.
medium.q: What does “refuge” mean in this passage?

answers: David both remembers deliverance and trusts the LORD
David is only describing a battle
challenge.explanation: David recalls how God delivered him and declares continuing confidence in Him.
challenge.q: What does the opening combination of thanksgiving and confidence show?

answers: The LORD is the source of protection and salvation
The LORD is far from David
challenge.explanation: The repeated titles emphasize God as David’s protector, refuge, and savior.
challenge.q: What central idea is repeated through David’s many titles for God?

challenge.explanation: A rock gives stability and a shield gives defense; both portray God’s protection.
challenge.q: How are “rock” and “shield” similar in David’s description?

easy.explanation: David speaks of the waves of death and floods of ungodly men surrounding him.
easy.q: What surrounded David in his distress?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “In my distress I called upon the LORD.”
easy.q: What did David do in his distress?

easy.explanation: David says that God heard his voice from His temple.
easy.q: What did the LORD do when David cried?

answers: The dangers and distress around him
medium.explanation: The deadly dangers described in these verses led David to cry to God.
medium.q: What caused David to call upon the LORD?

answers: They show that he was trapped and in danger
They show that he was joyful
They show that he was wealthy
medium.explanation: Waves, floods, sorrows, and snares create a picture of danger closing in around him.
medium.q: How do the images of waves and snares describe David’s condition?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes overwhelming and life-threatening distress.
medium.q: What does “the sorrows of hell compassed me about” mean in context?

answers: From danger and distress to God hearing David
challenge.explanation: The passage begins with danger and ends with David’s cry entering God’s ears.
challenge.q: What is the main movement in verses 5–7?

answers: They show that his trouble was severe and all around him
They prove that David had already died
challenge.explanation: The images make the urgency and seriousness of David’s distress clear.
challenge.q: Why do the repeated images of death strengthen David’s cry?

answers: God was attentive to David’s distress
David was speaking to his enemies
challenge.explanation: The expression emphasizes that God heard and received David’s plea.
challenge.q: What can be understood from “my cry did enter into his ears”?

paragraphs.title: The Storm of Revelation and Deliverance

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “Then the earth shook and trembled.”
easy.q: What happened to the earth when the LORD was angry?

answers: Smoke, fire, darkness, thunder, and lightning
easy.explanation: The passage describes smoke, fire, darkness, clouds, thunder, arrows, and lightning.
easy.q: Which signs appear in the description of the storm?

answers: He sent him into the sea
He drew him out of many waters
easy.explanation: God sent from above, took David, and drew him out of many waters.
easy.q: What did the LORD do for David amid the danger?

medium.explanation: The cosmic storm occurs because the LORD was wroth and displays His power.
medium.q: What does the storm reveal about the LORD?

answers: God sent, took David, and drew him out
medium.explanation: The passage says, “He sent from above, he took me; he drew me out of many waters.”
medium.q: What is the central sequence in the deliverance?

answers: Poetic imagery for the swift movement of the wind
medium.explanation: The phrase poetically pictures the wind carrying the LORD swiftly.
medium.q: What are “the wings of the wind” in this passage?

answers: A cosmic storm and a personal rescue
challenge.explanation: The LORD shakes creation, yet personally rescues David from the waters and his enemies.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in verses 8–20?

answers: It shows the immense power of the Deliverer
challenge.explanation: The greater the storm, the more clearly it displays the power of the God who saves David.
challenge.q: Why does the storm description strengthen the message of deliverance?

answers: God rescues David from both overwhelming danger and human enemies
David moved to live at sea
challenge.explanation: God’s rescue includes drawing David from the waters and delivering him from those who hated him.
challenge.q: What does the movement from “many waters” to “strong enemy” show?

paragraphs.title: David’s Righteousness and God’s Measure-for-Measure Justice

easy.explanation: David says, “The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness: according to the cleanness of my hands.”
easy.q: According to what did the LORD reward David?

easy.explanation: David says, “For I have kept the ways of the LORD.”
easy.q: What had David kept?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “And the afflicted people thou wilt save.”
easy.q: Whom will the LORD save according to verse 28?

answers: He says God rewarded him according to his righteousness
He says there is no connection
He says God punished his faithfulness
medium.explanation: David connects keeping God’s ways with the reward he received from the LORD.
medium.q: What connection does David make between faithfulness and reward?

answers: He responds with mercy to the merciful and judgment to the froward
He treats everyone in exactly the same way
medium.explanation: The passage describes God showing mercy to the merciful and dealing severely with the froward.
medium.q: How does the LORD respond to different kinds of people?

medium.explanation: “Froward” describes someone stubborn, perverse, or not upright.
medium.q: What does “froward” mean in this context?

answers: The LORD responds to people according to their ways
The LORD saves only the powerful
challenge.explanation: The LORD is described as merciful, upright, pure, or severe in relation to the person before Him.
challenge.q: What principle of divine government appears in verses 26–28?

answers: The afflicted are saved and the haughty are brought down
The afflicted are exalted and the proud are saved
challenge.explanation: God saves the afflicted but brings down the haughty.
challenge.q: What contrast appears at the end of the passage?

answers: To emphasize his continuing obedience to God’s commands
To say he did not know God’s law
challenge.explanation: David stresses that God’s judgments guided him and that he did not turn away from them.
challenge.q: Why does David mention God’s judgments being before him and his not departing from them?

paragraphs.title: The Light and Strength God Gives David

easy.explanation: David says, “For thou art my lamp, O LORD.”
easy.q: What is the LORD for David in verse 29?

answers: Run through a troop and leap over a wall
easy.explanation: David says, “For by thee I have run through a troop: by my God have I leaped over a wall.”
easy.q: What can David do through God?

easy.explanation: Verse 35 says, “He teacheth my hands to war.”
easy.q: What does God teach David’s hands to do?

answers: He lights his darkness and makes his way perfect
He hides the path from him
He sends him into battle without help
medium.explanation: God is David’s lamp, lightens his darkness, and makes his way perfect.
medium.q: How does God move David from darkness to confidence?

medium.explanation: God gives David the shield of salvation, and His gentleness makes David great.
medium.q: What do the shield and gentleness in verse 36 both describe?

answers: God gave him room and stability to walk securely
God made him unable to move
God sent him into the sea
medium.explanation: The following words explain that David’s feet did not slip.
medium.q: What does it mean that God enlarged David’s steps?

answers: It presents God as the source of guidance and ability
challenge.explanation: God’s light enables David to see and act confidently.
challenge.q: What is the function of the lamp image in verse 29?

answers: From a man in darkness to a strong and skilled warrior
From a warrior to a captive
From a king to a powerless man
challenge.explanation: God lights David, strengthens him, teaches him war, and keeps his steps steady.
challenge.q: How does David’s picture develop in verses 29–37?

challenge.explanation: The statement summarizes the stability God gives David in his path.
challenge.q: What does “my feet did not slip” emphasize?

easy.explanation: David says, “I have pursued mine enemies, and destroyed them.”
easy.q: What did David do to his enemies?

easy.explanation: Verse 39 says, “They are fallen under my feet.”
easy.q: What happened to the enemies after the pursuit?

easy.explanation: Verse 42 says they cried to the LORD, “but he answered them not.”
easy.q: Did the enemies receive an answer when they cried to the LORD?

answers: The great number of his enemies
medium.explanation: David says, “Thou hast girded me with strength to battle.”
medium.q: What enabled David to prevail in battle?

answers: The enemies retreat, are consumed, and fall
medium.explanation: God gives David the necks of his enemies, and they are destroyed and fall beneath him.
medium.q: What order of defeat is described?

answers: The enemies were placed under David’s power
medium.explanation: The expression pictures defeated enemies exposed to David’s power.
medium.q: What does “given me the necks of mine enemies” mean?

answers: The completeness and determination of David’s victory
An early end to the battle
challenge.explanation: David describes pursuing the enemies until they were completely defeated.
challenge.q: What does “I turned not again until I had consumed them” emphasize?

answers: God’s strength enables David to subdue them
challenge.explanation: The strength God supplies directly leads to David’s victory.
challenge.q: What is the connection between God girding David with strength and the enemies’ defeat?

answers: Their defeat is complete and they have no deliverer
challenge.explanation: Their final appeal fails, showing that their defeat is total.
challenge.q: What does the enemies’ unanswered cry imply?

paragraphs.title: David Raised to Head of Nations

easy.explanation: David says, “Thou also hast delivered me from the strivings of my people.”
easy.q: From what did the LORD deliver David?

easy.explanation: God kept David “to be head of the heathen.”
easy.q: What position did God preserve David to hold?

easy.explanation: The strangers submit themselves and become obedient when they hear David.
easy.q: How do strangers respond to David?

answers: God preserves and raises him to leadership
medium.explanation: God delivers David and keeps him in a position of authority over nations.
medium.q: What is the relationship between David’s deliverance and his becoming head of the heathen?

medium.explanation: The passage says, “as soon as they hear, they shall be obedient unto me.”
medium.q: What causes strangers to obey David?

medium.explanation: In context, the strangers lose strength and disappear as a threat.
medium.q: What does “fade away” mean in verse 46?

answers: He moves from internal conflict to leadership over nations
He moves from king to exile
He moves from rescuer to fugitive
challenge.explanation: God delivers him from the strivings of his people and makes him head of the heathen.
challenge.q: What change in David’s status appears in this passage?

answers: To show that they yield to David’s authority
To show that they defeat him
challenge.explanation: The two expressions reinforce the completeness of their submission.
challenge.q: Why are strangers described as both submitting and obeying?

answers: They emerge from fortified places in fear
challenge.explanation: Their close places suggest enclosed or fortified locations from which they come out trembling.
challenge.q: What does “out of their close places” suggest about the strangers?

paragraphs.title: Praise, Thanksgiving, and the Promise to David’s House

easy.explanation: Verse 47 begins, “The LORD liveth; and blessed be my rock.”
easy.q: How does David begin the closing praise?

answers: The building of his house only
easy.explanation: David thanks God for avenging him, delivering him, and lifting him above his enemies.
easy.q: For what does David give thanks?

easy.explanation: David says, “Therefore I will give thanks unto thee, O LORD, among the heathen.”
easy.q: Before whom will David give thanks?

answers: He brings him forth from enemies and lifts him above them
He hides him from his people
He delivers him to his enemies
medium.explanation: God brings David out from his enemies and lifts him above those who rise against him.
medium.q: What does God do for David according to verse 49?

answers: God’s deliverance gives David reason to thank and sing
medium.explanation: The word “Therefore” shows that David’s praise follows God’s saving acts.
medium.q: What is the connection between deliverance and praise?

answers: The king chosen and anointed by God
A man hiding in a fortress
medium.explanation: The verse identifies God’s anointed as David, the king.
medium.q: What does “his anointed” refer to in verse 51?

answers: It reaches among the nations, not only Israel
It is intended only for enemies
challenge.explanation: David promises to give thanks and sing among the heathen.
challenge.q: What is the scope of David’s thanksgiving at the end?

answers: It connects the deliverance with enduring mercy to David and his seed
challenge.explanation: The final verse extends God’s mercy beyond one victory to David and his descendants.
challenge.q: How does the ending expand the meaning of David’s personal deliverance?

answers: The continuing nature of God’s mercy
That David will immediately lose the kingdom
That the passage returns to the storm
challenge.explanation: “For evermore” presents God’s mercy as enduring beyond the immediate rescue.
challenge.q: What does “to David, and to his seed for evermore” emphasize?

paragraphs.title: Praise, Thanksgiving, and the Promise to David’s House

easy.explanation: David says, “The LORD liveth; and blessed be my rock,” referring to God.
easy.q: Who is David’s “rock”?

answers: Vengeance and victory over the nations
easy.explanation: God is the One who avenges David and brings people down under him.
easy.q: What does God give David according to verse 47?

answers: He gives thanks and sings praises
easy.explanation: David says, “I will give thanks unto thee… among the heathen, and I will sing praises.”
easy.q: What does David do among the heathen?

answers: God lives and saves, David gives thanks, and mercy continues
David is defeated and God disappears
medium.explanation: The ending moves from God’s life and salvation to David’s praise and enduring mercy.
medium.q: What sequence of ideas shapes the conclusion?

answers: To emphasize God as both stable refuge and source of salvation
To distinguish David from his enemies
medium.explanation: Both titles present God as David’s secure refuge and saving power.
medium.q: Why does David call God both his “rock” and the “God of the rock of my salvation”?

answers: God is a high and secure source of deliverance
medium.explanation: The phrase portrays God as a strong place and source of salvation for His king.
medium.q: What does “tower of salvation” mean?

answers: David’s success is presented as the result of God’s salvation and mercy
The kingdom is presented as accidental
challenge.explanation: God gives salvation to His king, lifts David up, and delivers him from the violent man.
challenge.q: How does the conclusion connect David’s kingship with God’s action?

answers: David’s thanksgiving will be proclaimed beyond Israel
challenge.explanation: The phrase suggests public and far-reaching praise among the nations.
challenge.q: What does praising God “among the heathen” imply?

answers: It gives David and his seed an enduring future of God’s mercy
It limits mercy to one moment
challenge.explanation: The phrase extends God’s mercy beyond the present victory into the future.
challenge.q: How does “for evermore” affect the ending?
